LESSON: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: DILEMMA NARRATIVES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the qualities of a good narrator?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative
2. recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives
3. appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: DILEMMA NARRATIVES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: DILEMMA NARRATIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives to a partner. (skill: recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative.
3. Practise this skill: recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the lessons learnt from the dilemma narrative for literary appreciation.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the qualities of a good narrator?
2. How can narratives contribute to decision making?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.4.1 Intensive reading: Dilemma Narratives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the characters in a given dilemma narrative.
5. Be able to: recognise a closing formula as a feature of dilemma narratives.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
